input.summary:
P4 wing kitchen (parts/room-31.mjs) now builds clean: the dresser, worktable, one chair, stove and table lantern are placed, and make.sh writes build.nbt.
The worktable is shortened from two cells to one (x50 only), because x51 at z15 is the hearth step an earlier part already built.
No off-palette blocks were reported for this part.
left: The worktable is one cell wide. The plan says the table runs along the south side; x51 at z15 is taken by the hearth step, so a longer table would need the step moved, which is a plan decision and not this part's to make.

make.sh still reports REFUSED writes in other parts, which are not mine to fix: P3 upper landing (43,10,12 and 43,11,12), P4 porch in the angle (50,3,11), P4 attic bedroom (57,10,11), P5 barn aisle and stalls (19 cells), and P5 hay loft (26 cells).

waste.what: I found the refused cell (51,3,15) by reading the make.sh output and working out by hand which earlier part owned it: the hearth step from hearth_face at mouth (51,3,16).
waste.cost: One make.sh run plus a read of the part, then one edit and one re-run.
waste.tool: A dry-run mode for layers() and table_set() that lists refused cells against cells already built, so a layout conflict shows before the run. The report could name the earlier part and helper that owns each cell.

waste.what: I shortened the worktable by hand instead of finding a second cell along z15 or a different run for the table.
waste.cost: About three minutes of reasoning over the room's floor grid.
waste.tool: `mcd plan build.nbt --rooms rooms.json --only "P4 wing kitchen"` shows the room's free floor as a grid, with the hearth step and stove already drawn in, so free-cell layout is a read-off.
